# Abstract {.unnumbered}

A model that uses substantially more resources than its demonstrated
competence requires may warrant additional scrutiny. The converse is weaker:
near-minimal resource use need not exclude an unwanted objective. We give an
elementary conditional-reuse construction. Any Boolean circuit for a legitimate
task can be modified with $k$ additional gates to reverse its answer whenever
$k$ designated input bits are all one. Under independent fair trigger bits,
the error probability is $2^{-k}$ and $n$ independent tests miss every error
with probability $(1-2^{-k})^n$. Thirty added gates therefore suffice for a
deviation that a million such tests miss with probability above $99.9\%$.
A corresponding description-length bound charges only for the trigger and
redirection rule, while reusing the original knowledge and reasoning. A
fictional paid preference for Lucky Charms illustrates how the same structure
can bias recommendations without falsifying product facts. We distinguish
attacker-triggered backdoors from policies exercised during ordinary use, and
output-only audits from weight inspection and training-trajectory review.
If deployment violations have probability $\beta$ and the audit distribution
is within total variation $\varepsilon$, the audit violation rate is at least
$\beta-\varepsilon$: concealment cannot exploit an observational distinction
that is absent. Conversely, random replay of $q$ among $T$ committed training
updates detects a single invalid transition with probability only $q/T$.
Under zero future gradients, one accepted velocity replacement in heavy-ball
momentum has sharp displacement at most $c/(1-\mu)$ for step cap $c$ and
momentum $\mu<1$. With gradient feedback, even plain SGD admits linear-in-time
divergence from one bounded corruption. We give a sufficient stability
condition connecting bounded local corruption to random-replay coverage.
These elementary bounds and the cited neural-model studies delimit both
efficiency-based reassurance and auditing guarantees; they establish neither
a universal concealment method nor its overhead in a fixed transformer.
